llm_narrative: Across the 500 evaluation tasks, qwen3.5_35b_output achieved a mean claim‑coverage of 0.2346 and a median of 0, with only 10.6 % of instances reaching the 75 % coverage threshold. Failure diagnostics flagged 472 cases (94.4 % of the sample), split almost evenly between tool‑driven errors (220 calls, 46.6 %) and pure cognitive lapses (252, 53.4 %). The most common root causes were selecting the wrong tool (123 occurrences) and misreading the task description (121), together accounting for more than half of all failures; no‑tool use (88) and early termination (84) were also prominent, while hallucinations and parsing errors were relatively rare. This pattern indicates that the model frequently initiates inappropriate or unnecessary tool calls and then aborts reasoning before integrating retrieved data, rather than struggling with complex inference per se. A concrete remediation is to embed a lightweight verification step after each tool invocation that checks whether the returned schema matches the expected fields and, if not, forces a re‑selection of the correct tool before proceeding. Compared with other models, qwen3.5_35b_output’s failure profile is distinguished by a high incidence of actionable tool‑misuse (≈26 % of all tasks) despite flawless run health, suggesting that its internal tool‑routing policy—not its underlying language capabilities—is the primary bottleneck.
